_comment: A2A TRANSACTION POLICY CONFIGURATION (Phase 7). Configuration, not rules.
The PAP pushes this document into OPA at data.agentic_iam.config.a2a, and
policies/a2a/transaction.rego reads it. The split is the one Phase 5.5 drew
for loan thresholds and Phase 6 drew for mandate bounds: what an amount
MEANS is a security rule a reviewer reads in Rego; what the numbers ARE is
a treasury decision a risk committee changes without touching a rule.
Nothing in Python reads these values. There is no `if amount > x` anywhere
in the application -- the PIP establishes the amount from the instruction
record and OPA decides what to do about it.
FAILING CLOSED: if this document is absent from the engine,
a2a/transaction.rego denies with A2A_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED rather than
falling through. An unconfigured threshold must never read as 'no limit'.
Amounts are whole rupees (INR), as integers. Canonical JSON refuses floats,
so a fractional amount cannot be signed in the first place.
agent_autonomous_limit_inr -- at or below this, a sending agent holding
a valid capability credential scoped to payment_instructions may have
its instruction carried out on its own authority. No human is involved,
because referring every small payment to a person produces
rubber-stamping, which is worse than not asking.
single_approver_limit_inr -- above the autonomous limit and at or below
this, ONE authorized PAYMENT_OFFICER must approve.
Above single_approver_limit_inr -- TWO distinct authorized humans. The
same person cannot satisfy both: the database refuses the second
sign-off, the artifact verifier refuses a document naming one person
twice, and a2a/transaction.rego counts the distinct approvers inside
the VERIFIED artifact rather than trusting a stored number.
Which human role may approve a payment. A DEDICATED role, deliberately
not LOAN_OFFICER: a loan officer's authority is over lending decisions,
and letting it extend to moving money would be privilege creep arriving
as a side effect. The RULE that reads it lives in
policies/control_plane/humans.rego.
Maker-checker. The officer named as submitted_by on the instruction may
not sign it off. Enforced by the SAME rule that enforces it for loans --
cp-humans reads data.agentic_iam.config.loan.separation_of_duties, so
the switch below is recorded for review and the live rule is the loan
one. Kept here so a reader of this file is not left believing payments
have their own switch.
WHICH ACTIONS MAY BE INSTRUCTED AGENT-TO-AGENT AT ALL. An allow-list,
never a deny-list: an action nobody has analysed for remote instruction
is not eligible, which is the safe direction for a list that will be
added to over time.
`execute_payment` on `payment_instructions` is the Phase 7 subject: one
agent asks another to settle a payment, the amount is material, and the
whole reconciliation chain has something real to run against.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: approve_loan, disburse_funds and override_decision.
Those are the Phase 5.5 human-approval actions on a DIFFERENT resource
with a DIFFERENT dual-control boundary, and letting an A2A instruction
reach them would mean one sender could drive the loan approval flow
through a channel it was never analysed for.
Also absent: `read`. An agent asking another agent to read a record on
its behalf is the confused-deputy shape, and it needs its own analysis
before it is enabled rather than being permitted because it looks
harmless.
execute_payment is NOT JIT-eligible, and is excluded BY NAME in
policies/data/jit_policy.json as well as by omission from that file's
allow-list. Two independent refusals, for the reason approve_loan has
two: a mandate carries an authorization forward across several actions,
and a human who approved one payment did not approve five.
Recorded here as well so an operator reading the A2A configuration
learns it without having to go and check the JIT one.
Recorded for review. The CEILING that is actually enforced is
A2A_MAX_TTL_SECONDS in application settings, applied during envelope
verification -- before OPA is reached, because an envelope with an
absurd window should be refused without a policy round trip. Policy
cannot be more permissive than it.
